overview.text: The Plains Garter Snake is a medium-sized, harmless garter snake of the central United States and southern Canada. It is one of the most cold-tolerant snakes and may come out to bask on warm winter days.

identification.text: A bright orange or yellow stripe from head to tail, greenish-yellow stripes on the sides, black bars on the lips, and usually light yellow spots on top of the head.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Great Plains and Midwest, from central Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba south to northern Texas and New Mexico, and east to Illinois and Indiana.

habitat.text: Meadows and prairies near water such as marshes, streams and ponds; also vacant lots and abandoned buildings in cities.

behaviour.text: Active from about April to late October. It mates in April or May near the shared winter den.

diet.text: Mainly earthworms, slugs and small amphibians.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young between August and October.

recognise.text: Orange or yellow stripe down the middle of the back.
